- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +5% above peak or apply mean reversion to 10-day moving average.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.3+), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use 14-day smoothed sentiment as proxy.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply 2–4% downward bias for first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.5 → +0.6), model fails to capture mean reversion; apply 1–2% downward correction after 3 consecutive positive sentiment days.
